samples.summary: Snap runs unconditionally over both axes on every shift, but no test covers the newly-reachable cross-axis / pre-existing-straddle repair
samples.evidence: `shiftWorksheetViewState` now calls `snapFreezePastMerges(..., ws.frozenRows, ws.frozenCols)` for *every* insert/delete, regardless of axis, so a row insert can now silently grow `frozenCols` (and vice versa), and a document that already contained a straddling merge (created before this invariant existed, or by any other writer) will have its freeze boundary jump on a completely unrelated edit far below/right of the boundary. All three new backend tests (worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:492-575) and both new sheets tests (test/workbook/worksheet-structure.test.ts:187-237) set up a straddle *caused by* the edit on the same axis; the negative test ("leaves the freeze alone when no block straddles it") has no pre-existing straddle and would pass even if the snap block were deleted. Nothing asserts the cross-axis or pre-existing-straddle outcome, so a regression there (or an unintended user-visible freeze jump) ships undetected.

samples.summary: New delete-snap test's expected value coincides with the initial freeze, so it cannot distinguish snapping from 'freeze never adjusted'
samples.evidence: The test seeds `setFreezePane(5, 0)` and asserts `frozenRows: 5` after `deleteRows(1, 1)`. It does fail if the snap is removed (the shrink leaves 4), but it passes unchanged if the shrink branch of `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1400-1412) stopped working at all, since 5 is also the untouched value. Its insert sibling (merge.test.ts:853-857) additionally asserts `store.getFreezePane()`; this one does not, so persistence of the delete path is unasserted. Choosing numbers where before != after would make the assertion sensitive to both branches.

samples.summary: Doc comment tells callers to read the snapped freeze back via `GET .../freeze`, but no test asserts that endpoint reports the snapped value
samples.evidence: The new doc block states "a successful insert or delete may leave the tab with more frozen rows or columns than it had; read them back with `GET .../freeze`". The new controller tests assert only the Yorkie document state (`doc.getRoot().sheets[TAB].frozenRows`), and the insert/delete responses echo only `{axis, index, count}`. I found no test in worksheet.controller.spec.ts or worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts that performs a freeze read after an insert/delete to prove the documented contract holds end-to-end.

finding.summary: The test claiming to cover the new freeze-snap inside `shiftCells` never triggers the snap
finding.evidence: `it('should keep the freeze clear of a block when rows are inserted')` merges A2:A4, calls setFreezePane(2,0) (already snapped to 4 by `setFreezePane`), then `insertRows(1, 1)`. In `shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1392-1417) the pre-existing branch `count > 0 && index <= frozen` already yields frozenRows = 5, and the shifted block A3:A5 satisfies range[1].r (5) > rows (5) === false, so `snapFreezePastMerges` at sheet.ts:1422 makes no change. The asserted `{ frozenRows: 5, frozenCols: 0 }` holds identically with the whole new snap block deleted — it is fake coverage for that block. No test in the diff or in packages/sheets/test/sheet/freeze-pane.test.ts drives a structural edit that actually leaves a block straddling the boundary (e.g. deleting rows inside the frozen area so a block ends up half-frozen, or inserting rows inside a block that sits on the boundary), which is exactly the state the new code exists to prevent.

verdict.reason: The test the finding names does not exist: grep for "keep the freeze clear" / "when rows are inserted" finds no such test in packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts or anywhere in the repo. The closest test, merge.test.ts:815 'should carry a frozen block down with an insert above it', is explicitly documented in its own comment (lines 825-827) as the case where the pre-existing boundary adjustment suffices and "no snapping needed" — it is not presented as coverage for the new snap. More decisively, the claimed gap ("no test drives a structural edit that actually leaves a block straddling the boundary") is false: merge.test.ts:833-858 seeds a straddling block via the store/load path and asserts frozenRows 6 after insertRows (pre-existing branch alone yields 4, and persistence to the store is asserted too); merge.test.ts:860-877 covers the delete branch (frozen shrinks to 4, block slides to A2:A5, asserts 5); merge.test.ts:879-893 covers the column axis (asserts frozenCols 5 where the branch alone gives 3); merge.test.ts:895-909 covers the multi-pass cascade in snapFreezePastMerges. I traced each against sheet.ts:1391-1423 and merging.ts:207-233 — every one of these assertions changes value if the snap block at sheet.ts:1418-1423 is removed, so they are load-bearing, not vacuous.
